  HIGH     F1   No IPv4 firewall rules are loaded                                                -25
                iptables-save shows no tables for IPv4, so nothing is filtered: every port of the
                host is open, and the host forwards packets without a filter when routing is on.
                fix  Load a rule set for IPv4. The recommended baseline is a complete one; its notes
                     say how to apply it with a way back.
                     Write the baseline for IPv4 to a file:
                       iptables-analyzer --baseline=4 > baseline.v4

  HIGH     F2   No IPv6 firewall rules are loaded                                                -10
                ip6tables-save shows no tables, and IPv4 rules do not filter IPv6. Hosts usually get
                IPv6 addresses automatically; every service that listens on IPv6 is then open.
                fix  Load a rule set for IPv6. The recommended baseline is a complete one; its notes
                     say how to apply it with a way back.
                     Write the baseline for IPv6 to a file:
                       iptables-analyzer --baseline=6 > baseline.v6

  HIGH     F3   sshd is open to any source on 22/tcp                                              -5
                No rule names the port: INPUT accepts it from any source by default. Close the
                default first; then accept each port that must stay reachable, for its clients only.
